sources.title: Ranil Wickremesinghe: historical parliamentary profile and qualifications
sources.findings: Read parliamentary profile: birth 24 March 1949, LLB and legal professional qualifications. The legislative table begins with the 1977 assembly and ends with the 2021–2022 parliamentary period; its MP heading is historical. A stale narrative says continuous service from 1978 for 28 years and is not used as current evidence. The table confirms prime minister from 12 May 2022 and finance/economic-stabilisation portfolio from 25 May. Its 2021 membership start is 18 June, whereas the election news item describes 23 June; the profile uses the year only and does not conflate selection, gazetting and oath. Conflicting fine-grained historical portfolio dates are not silently resolved.

sources.title: Parliament elects Wickremesinghe president, 20 July 2022
sources.findings: Read Parliament’s 20 July 2022 election account: 134 votes for Wickremesinghe, 82 for Alahapperuma and three for Dissanayake; 223 cast, four invalid, two abstentions. This elected him to complete the predecessor’s term, not a fresh direct mandate. It corroborates 1977 entry, first premiership 7 May 1993–19 August 1994, subsequent terms and 12 May 2022 return. Its claim of full foreign-minister office at age 28 conflicts with the party biography’s deputy post; the deputy designation is retained. The page calls itself unedited and refers readers to Hansard. Its acting-president chronology and some 2015 dates are treated cautiously and not used to override gazettes.

sources.title: No. 2289/39: assumption of the presidency, 21 July 2022
sources.findings: Read original Gazette No. 2289/39 of 21 July 2022: elected by Parliament on 20 July; assumed office on 21 July for the unexpired period following Gotabaya Rajapaksa’s 14 July resignation. Eighth executive president is a narrower count than ninth president overall; no conflicting ordinal is used in the profile. The direct proclamation takes precedence over later summaries that put the oath on 22 July. Earlier acting powers are distinct from this assumption of the elected presidency.

sources.title: No. 2403/03: Dissanayake’s election, term commencement and oath, September 2024
sources.findings: Read original Gazette No. 2403/03 of 23 September 2024: Dissanayake was declared elected on 22 September; his term commenced on 22 September under Article 31(4); he took the oath and assumed office on 23 September under the stated constitutional provisions. The timeline records the 23 September transition while explicitly preserving the 22 September term start. It does not assume Wickremesinghe won a fresh term or remained president until the November parliamentary election. The five-year successor term is a legal term, not proof of future completion.

sources.publisher: Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs; archived by USIP
sources.title: Jan Petersen’s ceasefire announcement, 22 February 2002
sources.findings: Read the Norwegian foreign minister’s 22 February 2002 announcement archived in USIP’s Peace Agreements Digital Collection: signed government/LTTE document deposited with Norway, ceasefire effective 00:00 on 23 February. Agreement and announcement are distinct from entry into force. Its aim was to support negotiation, not certify permanent peace or all parties’ later compliance. No casualty total or unsupported personal achievement claim is added. The archived statement is the date evidence; the separate agreement text supplies the structure, not a guessed signature date.

sources.title: Wickremesinghe sworn in again as prime minister, 16 December 2018
sources.findings: Read Sky News report dated 16 December 2018: Wickremesinghe was sworn in for a fifth time after Sirisena had replaced him with Mahinda Rajapaksa in October; parliamentary confidence disputes and court proceedings formed the background. His claim that removal was unlawful remains attributed. No full 2018 court docket was examined and no personal criminal verdict is inferred. A separate Daily Mirror report corroborates the oath but contains conflicting court dates and an impossible prorogation sequence; those details are not adopted.

sources.title: Approval of the 48-month Extended Fund Facility, 20 March 2023
sources.findings: Read IMF approval account dated 20 March 2023: 48-month EFF arrangement, SDR 2.286 billion, about US$3 billion at approval; immediate access to SDR 254 million, about US$333 million. Approval, immediate access and full disbursement are different. Macroeconomic and debt stability, fiscal reforms, governance and protection of vulnerable groups are program objectives, not proof they were already achieved. The party page’s early-March/US$330 million shorthand is replaced by the IMF record. Forecast table entries are not treated as actual 2026 outcomes.

sources.title: Sri Lanka’s recovery remains uneven, dated 6 October 2026
sources.findings: Read World Bank release with body date 6 October 2026, despite URL path 2 October. It reports recovery of aggregate output but lagging household income and labour-market outcomes. It spans administrations and is not a causal attribution to Wickremesinghe or evidence he remained in office. The 4.4% annual growth figure is a projection, not a completed-year result. CMS fields contain unrelated Bahamas and placeholder-like metadata; country and date are taken from the substantive Sri Lanka text. No unverified country-classification claim or cross-methodology poverty comparison is used.

sources.title: Former president arrested over alleged misuse of public funds, 22 August 2025
sources.findings: Read AP report of the 22 August 2025 arrest for alleged public-funds misuse during a UK stopover. This records allegations and custody, not guilt. The profile does not infer conviction or continuing detention in 2026 from the 2025 report.

sources.title: Court appearance and adjournment for Attorney General’s advice, 11 November 2026
sources.findings: Read Bhagya Silva’s 11 November 2026 Daily Mirror article body, not reader comments or its AI-summary interface. It reports Wickremesinghe and former presidential secretary Saman Ekanayake before Colombo Fort Acting Magistrate Kinsley Hettiarachchi and adjournment to 9 December for the Attorney General’s advice. This supports reported recent activity and an unresolved procedural stage; the December hearing has not yet occurred at the cutoff. No charge-sheet, final judgment, judicial transcript or original video was inspected.

sources.title: Historical biography of Ranil Wickremesinghe
sources.findings: Read UNP historical biography: six occasions as prime minister; first appointment after Premadasa’s assassination and during Wijetunga’s presidency; 2001–2004 and later terms; 2020–2021 parliamentary interruption; early deputy foreign-minister, youth and education roles. The page has dated presidential wording and self-promotional achievements, so it is not used to claim current presidency or independently measured economic/educational success. Its overall presidential ordinal differs from the gazette’s executive-presidency count. Its IMF timing and amounts are superseded by the fund’s own record.
